content.comment_body: I have two [product_name] devices and want to display values from both on the [product_name] interface panel. Is this achievable, and if so, how? I’m new to using the [product_name] interface.

The interface panel can only connect to one [product_name] device at a time. If you wish to see messages from both devices and perform functions, you can either select the appropriate device’s IP address in the interface menu, or transfer the second device’s data using a VM area to the first, then display messages for both on the first device.

How do I transfer data from the second [product_name] using VM area to the first one? Which method is simpler—menu selection on the panel or data transfer? What would you recommend? Thanks for your help.
Using the menu to select the device on the interface panel is easier. If you add both devices’ IP addresses to the selection menu, you can simply switch between them by choosing the appropriate IP.
I haven’t created a menu before. Any ideas on how to approach this? I want three menu pages for each device. Also, how can I make options to increase or decrease values?
Here is a possible suggestion for setting up your menus.
Thank you! Can the same menu layout be used for both devices? Also, can I adjust the value to increments like 0.10 seconds?

If you want to use one menu for both devices in a single [product_name], that’s not possible—the menus need to be tailored. The suggestion just guides your setup. However, each device can have its own menu.
So if I create two menus, one per device, can I just select the IP on the interface panel and it will work?
Yes, that would work.
Thank you, [user_name], this was very useful!
How did you create this? When I tried pasting the menu into my program, it disappeared.
What version of [product_name] programming tool do you use? [version_no] or [version_no]?
I’m using [version_no].
[version_no] has an issue when deleting or backspacing in I/O state names. To remove entries, set the cursor at the first letter and use the spacebar until the text is erased.
I was curious about how the ‘<’ arrow works, because when I pasted the menu into my program, the arrow was missing.
Do you mean copying and pasting a message text from my project into yours? If you only copy the message text, the references might be lost and the I/O state name won’t be included.
I tried several times to copy and paste. :P I’d like to add the '<' arrow but I'm unsure how you did it.
I’ll record a screen video for you. It’s too large for a single attachment, so I’m dividing it into a ZIP archive. Here’s the first part.
Here’s the second file. Download both to the same folder. After downloading, rename "I_O_state_name.z01.zip" to "I_O_state_name.z01". Then, unpack "I_O_state_name.zip" to view the video.
Thanks! Now I get how it works. I appreciate you explaining it with a video. Why can’t I click OK?
Have you reviewed the instructions?
Oh, sorry! I managed to get it working now. Thanks again for your help.
Consider editing your posts only afterward if needed. I saw them by chance—otherwise, modified posts might not appear as new.
Okay, I’ll remember that for future posts!
A new question by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled Change values with F3 F4 button. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to monitor and interact with two [product_name] devices through a single interface panel but learns that only one device can be accessed at a time. Switching between devices requires selecting their IP addresses in the panel menu. There’s some uncertainty about menu creation, navigation setup, and value adjustment across devices. The user faces challenges in reusing menu templates and navigating limitations of the configuration software and hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to control and view values from both devices on a single interface panel, either simultaneously or with a convenient switching method. They also seek simple menu configuration that can apply to both devices, along with the ability to adjust values in small increments.
